newsitem.title: USA: Minn. school funds stable despite dispute - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Minn. school funds stable despite dispute - Moody's.

text.p: Minnesota's school districts continue to have a stable financial outlook despite the dispute between Gov. Arne Carlson and lawmakers over the $6.7 billion biennium budget, Moody's Investors Service said Tuesday.
Carlson has called legislators back for a special session on Thursday to resolve the impasse over elementary and secondary school funding for the fiscal biennium beginning next week.

"Should this issue not be resolved prior to the new fiscal year, which begins July 1, Moody's expects no impact on Minnesota school districts' credit quality because the district's will continue to receive on average approximately 93 percent of the prior year's state aid funding level," Moody's said.

Carlson vetoed the two-year spending plan earlier in June because it lacked $150 million of tuition tax credits he has proposed. The governor's plan would triple current deductions and all credits to be used for hiring a tutor, summer school programs, purchase of a home computer for educational needs or tuition to private schools.

The fund and cash positions of Minnesota and most school districts are strong and state law allows districts to seek accelerated aid payments if necessary, Moody's said. No such applications have been made thus far, Moody's added.

Bonds issued under the Aa1-rated Minnesota School District Credit Enhancement program are also insulated from adverse effects from delayed payments as state law requires Minnesota to ensure timely debt service payments from the general fund if necessary, Moody's said.
